- 2025-10-20 · [Pixels may be better LLM inputs than text tokens](ideas/2025-10-20-pixels-may-be-better-llm-inputs-than-text.md) — Rendering all input as images could compress context, carry bold and colour, allow bidirectional attention and remove the tokenizer. *(view)*
- 2025-10-20 · [Text diffusion is a bidirectional transformer that re-masks a token canvas](ideas/2025-10-20-text-diffusion-is-bidirectional-denoising.md) — Without the maths, text diffusion is a bidirectional transformer that refreshes all tokens over noise steps; autoregression only appends. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [AI will blend into the same 2% growth curve](ideas/2025-10-17-agi-blends-into-gdp-growth.md) — Like computers and phones, AI will diffuse slowly and not show as a jump; the intelligence explosion has been happening for decades. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [To learn something, build it yourself without copy-paste](ideas/2025-10-17-build-it-yourself-no-copy-paste.md) — Writing the code from scratch, only looking at a reference, shows what you do not understand; blog posts and slides do not.
- 2025-10-17 · [Build for the capability that exists; a real tutor is a high bar](ideas/2025-10-17-calibrate-to-what-ai-can-do-tutor.md) — A good tutor finds your level and serves what fits; chat models do not yet, so build with AI in the loop and say when not to use AI.
- 2025-10-17 · [Coding agents are weak on novel code](ideas/2025-10-17-coding-agents-weak-on-novel-code.md) — In October 2025 he found agents good for boilerplate and tested ports but poor on unusual code, and preferred autocomplete for precise work. *(superseded)*
- 2025-10-17 · [Coding came first because it is text with diff tools](ideas/2025-10-17-coding-first-text-and-diffs.md) — Code is plain text with editors and diffs already built, so agents fit it; slides and other visual work lack a way to show changes. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [This is the decade of agents, not the year of agents](ideas/2025-10-17-decade-of-agents-not-year.md) — Agents are useful today but lack memory, multimodality and reliability; he expects about ten years of work before they match a good intern. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [The likely risk is a gradual loss of control and understanding](ideas/2025-10-17-gradual-loss-of-control-and-understanding.md) — He expects fewer people to understand systems built by AI, and many competing autonomous agents, rather than one machine taking over. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [Learn on demand through projects, then explain it to others](ideas/2025-10-17-learn-on-demand-then-explain.md) — Alternate project-driven learning with broad study, and re-explain what you learn; you find the gaps when you cannot explain.
- 2025-10-17 · [LLMs still lack culture and self-play](ideas/2025-10-17-llms-lack-culture-and-self-play.md) — Two multi-agent ideas are unclaimed: models writing notes for other models, and models posing problems for each other to solve. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [Teach by building ramps to knowledge](ideas/2025-10-17-ramps-to-knowledge.md) — Find the first-order core, show it in the smallest working code, and order material so each step needs only the one before; show the pain before the fix.
- 2025-10-17 · [Reinforcement learning sucks supervision through a straw](ideas/2025-10-17-rl-supervision-through-a-straw.md) — Outcome-only RL rewards every step of a lucky run equally; it works better than imitation but is noisy and needs new ideas such as reflection. *(view)*
- 2025-10-17 · [Share your beginner questions to an LLM with the author](ideas/2025-10-17-share-dumb-llm-questions-with-experts.md) — Put the paper in an LLM's context, ask your naive questions, and share the thread; it shows authors where beginners get lost.
- 2025-10-17 · [Model outputs are silently collapsed, so synthetic data needs entropy](ideas/2025-10-17-synthetic-data-and-model-collapse.md) — Each sample from a model looks fine but the set is narrow; training on your own output makes models worse, so seek outside variety.
- 2025-10-17 · [Weights are a hazy memory; the context window is working memory](ideas/2025-10-17-weights-hazy-memory-context-working-memory.md) — A model recalls training data vaguely but reads its context directly, so paste the source text instead of asking it to remember.
- 2025-10-14 · [Measure a project's weight with its lockfile, and rewrite heavy parts small](ideas/2025-10-14-count-dependencies-with-the-lockfile.md) — Count lockfile lines as a quick proxy for total dependencies, and when a small task drags in heavy infrastructure, write a short clean version yourself.
- 2025-10-13 · [Ask contributors to disclose LLM-written code they do not understand](ideas/2025-10-13-ai-contribution-disclosure-policy.md) — nanochat's AI policy is disclosure: a PR must declare parts with substantial LLM contribution that the author did not write or does not fully understand.
- 2025-10-13 · [Making a model know your own data is still research; use retrieval for now](ideas/2025-10-13-making-a-model-know-you-is-still-research.md) — Training a small model on your notes gives slop; a real personal model needs synthetic rewrites and a big finetune, so retrieval is the practical choice. *(view)*
- 2025-10-13 · [Keep the codebase minimal and forkable, with one dial](ideas/2025-10-13-nanochat-one-dial-minimal-fork.md) — nanochat avoids configuration frameworks; one integer (depth) sets all other hyperparameters, and changes must work at every depth.
- 2025-10-08 · [Models write over-defensive error handling](ideas/2025-10-08-models-over-defensive-about-exceptions.md) — After RL, models wrap code in try/except and fallbacks, so tell the agent to let errors surface.
- 2025-10-01 · [Finetune a small model to narrow the scope of one pipeline step](ideas/2025-10-01-finetune-small-model-for-narrow-scope.md) — Finetuning is less about style and more about narrowing scope; a small tuned model can beat a long few-shot prompt on one step of an LLM pipeline.
- 2025-10-01 · [LLMs are ghosts, not animals](ideas/2025-10-01-llms-are-ghosts-not-animals.md) — Frontier LLMs are statistical distillations of human text, a different kind of mind from animals; pretraining is a stand-in for evolution, not a copy of it. *(view)*
- 2025-10-01 · [For deep reading, put the whole text in the context window](ideas/2025-10-01-put-the-whole-text-in-context-not-rag.md) — Tools that retrieve chunks may drop what matters; paste the full sources into one chat so the model sees all of it, then fork the chat to ask more.
- 2025-09-25 · [Jobs change before they vanish, and supervision grows](ideas/2025-09-25-ai-and-jobs-radiologists-and-engineers.md) — Jobs are bundles of tasks; closed, repetitive digital work automates first, and people move toward supervising teams of imperfect AIs. *(view)*
- 2025-09-05 · [Get a second opinion from a stronger model on hard problems](ideas/2025-09-05-give-it-your-hardest-problems.md) — When one coding agent is stuck, a different, stronger model may solve the problem in minutes; then hand the result back.
- 2025-08-31 · [A quoted tilde is not expanded, so check an agent's delete commands](ideas/2025-08-31-quote-paths-and-check-agent-rm-commands.md) — In shell quotes, "~" stays a literal folder name; an unquoted rm -rf ~ meant for that folder deletes your home folder instead.
- 2025-08-27 · [RL environments are the new training data](ideas/2025-08-27-rl-environments-are-the-new-data.md) — Pretraining used web text, finetuning used conversations, and RL uses environments where models act and see outcomes.
- 2025-08-24 · [Stitch several coding tools together, by task size](ideas/2025-08-24-stitch-coding-tools-by-task.md) — In August 2025 he used tab-complete for most edits, an agent for big easy chunks and a stronger model for hard bugs, and found agents lacked taste. *(superseded)*
- 2025-08-20 · [Flatten a repository into one page for humans and LLMs](ideas/2025-08-20-render-repo-for-humans-and-llms.md) — rendergit turns a git repo into one static HTML page with a human view and an LLM view of the same code as plain text to paste into a model.
- 2025-08-09 · [Models are too agentic by default, so state stakes and scope](ideas/2025-08-09-models-too-agentic-state-stakes-and-scope.md) — Tuned models over-think simple questions and search the whole repo, so tell them the scope and the depth you want.
- 2025-07-14 · [Read a few cases in depth, not only dashboards](ideas/2025-07-14-study-a-few-cases-not-dashboards.md) — Close study of a few random cases teaches more than aggregate statistics over all cases; both help, but the aggregate view is overused.
- 2025-07-10 · [Write new knowledge for AI readers, not as a PDF](ideas/2025-07-10-write-research-for-llms-not-pdf.md) — As AI can infer what is already online, people's main contribution is original results; publish them as repos, CSVs and markdown that LLMs can read.
- 2025-07-05 · [Write small, modular, copy-paste code like bacteria do](ideas/2025-07-05-write-code-like-bacteria.md) — Code that is small, modular and self-contained spreads easily; write functions someone can copy without new imports, and keep a big monorepo only where needed.
- 2025-06-30 · [Recursive self-improvement has already begun](ideas/2025-06-30-recursive-self-improvement-is-already-underway.md) — Self-improvement is not a sudden event; tools like IDEs, git and LLM completion have sped up building the next version for years, and nanoGPT is a fair test. *(view)*
- 2025-06-27 · [A small cognitive core that reasons and looks facts up](ideas/2025-06-27-the-llm-cognitive-core.md) — A model of about a billion to a few billion parameters could keep the reasoning skills, drop most memorised facts, look things up, and run on every device. *(view)*
- 2025-06-26 · [The bitter lesson as "turn the crank"](ideas/2025-06-26-the-bitter-lesson-turn-the-crank.md) — Prefer methods that improve when you give them more compute without edits; break the rule on purpose only when you can afford to miss the next crank. *(view)*
- 2025-06-25 · [Put the answer first and spend effort when you write](ideas/2025-06-25-answer-first-compute-at-creation-time.md) — Write the specific ask or result first and the context after it, and spend more effort when you write so that readers spend less.
- 2025-06-25 · [Context engineering, not prompt engineering](ideas/2025-06-25-context-engineering.md) — The skill is filling the context window with the right information for the next step, plus specs, tools and workflows, not polishing one prompt.
- 2025-06-20 · [What is the best possible pretraining data?](ideas/2025-06-20-what-is-the-best-pretraining-data-stream.md) — Imagine a pure-quality data stream, maybe textbook-like markdown, and ask how strong a 1B model on 10B tokens could be; today's data is messy. *(view)*
- 2025-06-17 · [A demo is the first nine; each next nine costs the same work](ideas/2025-06-17-demo-to-product-gap-march-of-nines.md) — A system that works 90% of the time is a demo; reaching 99.999% takes years, so be sceptical of demos and agent timelines.
- 2025-06-17 · [LLMs are like 1960s operating systems](ideas/2025-06-17-llms-are-1960s-operating-systems.md) — The LLM is a new computer whose context is memory; it runs time-shared in the cloud, with text as its only interface for now. *(view)*
- 2025-06-17 · [LLMs are people spirits with superpowers and deficits](ideas/2025-06-17-llms-are-people-spirits-with-deficits.md) — An LLM simulates people, so it recalls like a savant, is jagged, forgets everything between sessions and can be tricked; work around all four.
- 2025-06-17 · [Build partial-autonomy apps with an autonomy slider](ideas/2025-06-17-partial-autonomy-and-autonomy-slider.md) — Good LLM apps manage context, chain model calls, give a GUI for fast checking and let the user set how much the AI does.
- 2025-06-17 · [Software 3.0 means programming computers in English](ideas/2025-06-17-software-3-0-english-as-programs.md) — Code is Software 1.0, trained weights are 2.0, and an LLM's context window is 3.0; learn all three and pick the right one per task.
- 2025-06-16 · [Agent security is the wild west](ideas/2025-06-16-agent-security-is-the-wild-west.md) — Prompt injection is like early computer viruses; risk peaks with local agents and with chat connectors, and agents need narrow actions, not free bash.
- 2025-06-11 · [When the prior overwhelms the likelihood](ideas/2025-06-11-when-the-prior-overwhelms-the-likelihood.md) — A model can read what it expects instead of what is in the input, as when it answered a classic illusion question about an image that had no illusion. *(view)*
- 2025-06-05 · [Either the automation adapts, or the world does](ideas/2025-06-05-automation-meets-the-task-or-the-task-meets-it.md) — Automation adapts to the tasks or the tasks adapt to it, usually both; he expects software to adapt about 80% and hardware to adapt little. *(view)*
- 2025-06-04 · [Opaque, binary-format tools do not fit human and AI work](ideas/2025-06-04-opaque-binary-uis-are-ngmi.md) — Tools with rich UIs, no scripting and binary formats are at risk, because an AI must be able to read and script the tools it works with.
- 2025-06-04 · [Verification, not generation, is the bottleneck](ideas/2025-06-04-verification-not-generation-is-the-bottleneck.md) — Creating has a generate step and a discriminate step; LLMs made the first instant, so coding speed now depends on cutting the cost of checking.
- 2025-06-02 · [Generated video can be optimised directly](ideas/2025-06-02-video-generation-is-directly-optimizable.md) — Video from a neural net can be optimised against any goal, such as engagement, which may make feeds far more addictive than ranking human-made clips. *(view)*
- 2025-05-25 · [Prompting was the unlock he missed in 2015](ideas/2025-05-25-prompting-was-the-unlock-he-missed.md) — In 2015 he missed that one set of weights could do many tasks if you just ask; a blind spot like this can move timelines more than new evidence. *(view)*
- 2025-05-10 · [System prompt learning, where the model writes its own lessons](ideas/2025-05-10-system-prompt-learning.md) — A missing learning paradigm: after a task, the model reviews what happened and writes explicit lessons into its own system prompt, later distilled into weights.
- 2025-05-06 · [Learn the physical lens of computing](ideas/2025-05-06-learn-the-physical-lens-of-computing.md) — Study how computers use energy, data locality, parallelism and architecture, not only computability and complexity; the physical lens gives power. *(view)*
- 2025-04-30 · [Leaderboards get gamed; watch real usage](ideas/2025-04-30-leaderboards-get-gamed-watch-real-usage.md) — A top rank on a public arena can mean the lab tuned for the arena. Trust your own use and real-usage signals such as OpenRouter rankings.
- 2025-04-27 · [Tic-tac-toe is harder for LLMs than it looks](ideas/2025-04-27-tic-tac-toe-is-harder-for-llms-than-it-looks.md) — Models fail at tic-tac-toe because it needs line checks and look-ahead that humans do with their eyes and a sheet of paper. *(view)*
- 2025-04-27 · [Vibe coding a real app is easy locally and hard to ship](ideas/2025-04-27-vibe-coding-real-app-lessons.md) — A local prototype appears in minutes; real deployment hits stale model knowledge, rate limits, secrets and subtle design bugs that you must still catch.
- 2025-04-26 · [Go back to RSS, with a feed you control](ideas/2025-04-26-rss-reader-with-llm-feed.md) — RSS is open and hackable and escapes engagement slop; a good reader would add social features and an LLM-built feed that you customise.
- 2025-04-24 · [Keep the AI on a tight leash for code you care about](ideas/2025-04-24-ai-assisted-coding-rhythm.md) — Review is the bottleneck, so work in small, specific steps: give context, compare approaches, review, test and commit each change.
- 2025-04-07 · [LLMs reverse the usual path of technology diffusion](ideas/2025-04-07-llms-reverse-technology-diffusion.md) — Most technologies reach governments and firms first; LLMs help ordinary people most, because they give broad, shallow expertise at almost no cost. *(view)*
- 2025-04-06 · [Write boring code with NASA-style rules](ideas/2025-04-06-write-boring-code-with-nasa-style-rules.md) — To make C safer, remove clever features: ban anything exotic and keep every line to one plain action, as NASA's rules for C code do.
- 2025-04-04 · [Move AI predictions to betting markets](ideas/2025-04-04-move-ai-predictions-to-betting-markets.md) — Turn AI forecasts into betting-market questions, but each one needs a concrete, resolvable predicate; evals and GDP make weak ones. *(view)*
- 2025-03-31 · [Text chat is the terminal era; ask for visual output](ideas/2025-03-31-text-chat-is-the-terminal-era.md) — Chat with a model is like typing at a 1980s console; people take in images, layouts and HTML faster, so ask models to answer visually.
- 2025-03-27 · [Building a web app is like assembling IKEA furniture; make it just work for AIs](ideas/2025-03-27-web-app-stack-is-ikea-furniture.md) — A web app needs a dozen separate services; the hard part is configuration, not code, and whoever makes it work out of the box for people and AIs wins. *(view)*
- 2025-03-23 · [Build a small app in a language you do not know, one chat step at a time](ideas/2025-03-23-build-an-app-in-a-language-you-do-not-know.md) — He shipped a working iPhone app in about an hour with no Swift experience, by following a chat with small steps; past 400 lines the chat started to struggle.
- 2025-03-19 · [Keep one note you append to and review](ideas/2025-03-19-append-and-review-note.md) — One text note, new items added on top, old items sinking, and a periodic skim that rescues what still matters, covers most note-taking needs.
- 2025-03-12 · [Build docs and tools for agents, which curl instead of click](ideas/2025-03-12-write-docs-for-llms.md) — The main user of your product or docs is becoming an LLM agent, so ship markdown docs, a CLI or API, and skills, not only pages to click.
- 2025-02-27 · [Ask the model for a conceptual diagram of what you read](ideas/2025-02-27-ask-for-a-diagram-of-what-you-read.md) — Ask for a conceptual diagram of a chapter or code; the model writes Mermaid code that renders as a tree you can remember.
- 2025-02-27 · [Bigger pretraining improves everything a little, and is hard to point to](ideas/2025-02-27-bigger-pretraining-helps-everything-a-little.md) — A model with 10X more pretraining compute gets better in diffuse ways: knowledge, nuance, humor; test it on non-reasoning tasks, and do not trust a small poll. *(view)*
- 2025-02-27 · [Check which tools the model has before you trust its answer](ideas/2025-02-27-check-which-tools-the-model-has.md) — Search and a code interpreter fix recent facts and hard arithmetic; models without them guess, so ask for the tool.
- 2025-02-27 · [Try a fast model first, switch to a thinking model for hard problems](ideas/2025-02-27-fast-model-first-thinking-model-for-hard.md) — Know which model and tier you use; start fast, move to a reasoning model for hard code and math, and compare several vendors.
- 2025-02-27 · [Give examples in prompts, and save the prompts you reuse](ideas/2025-02-27-few-shot-prompts-and-saved-instructions.md) — A description plus a few concrete examples raises accuracy; save repeated prompts as custom GPTs or custom instructions.
- 2025-02-27 · [Start a new chat when the topic changes](ideas/2025-02-27-fresh-chat-per-topic.md) — Old context distracts the model and costs more per token, so reset when the topic changes; the lasting fix is context managed by the agent.
- 2025-02-27 · [Treat LLM output as a first draft and check the sources](ideas/2025-02-27-llm-output-is-a-first-draft.md) — Even with search or deep research, answers can be wrong; use citations, primary sources and a read of the generated code.
- 2025-02-27 · [Ask the model to write a small app just for you](ideas/2025-02-27-one-off-apps-on-demand.md) — Instead of finding an app, have the model write a tiny local one, such as a flashcard quiz, and run it in the chat.
- 2025-02-24 · [Agency matters more than intelligence, and is scarcer](ideas/2025-02-24-agency-matters-more-than-intelligence.md) — He once had this backwards; the drive to take initiative is more powerful and rarer than raw intelligence, so hire and educate for it. *(view)*
- 2025-02-18 · [Three breakthroughs so far; autonomous agents need a few more](ideas/2025-02-18-three-breakthroughs-more-leaps-needed.md) — Task evals are easy to serve and beat; long-running autonomous work, which people mean by AGI, needs research leaps beyond scaling. *(view)*
- 2025-02-14 · [Pack your project into one prompt for a quick, scoped question](ideas/2025-02-14-package-repo-into-one-prompt.md) — When coding agents over-explore, bundle a small repo into one prompt, start a new chat, ask one question at the end and pick the model yourself.
- 2025-02-12 · [Invisible Unicode characters can smuggle data and prompts into an LLM](ideas/2025-02-12-invisible-unicode-can-hide-prompts.md) — Variation selectors can hide arbitrary bytes behind one visible emoji; they cost many tokens and can carry a hidden prompt injection.
- 2025-02-07 · [Make a long from-scratch intro to your own field](ideas/2025-02-07-make-a-from-scratch-intro-in-your-own-field.md) — A multi-hour, from-scratch walkthrough by an expert is a format he wants in every field, and the tools to make one are simple.
- 2025-02-02 · [Vibe coding is fine for throwaway projects](ideas/2025-02-02-vibe-coding-for-throwaway-projects.md) — Vibe coding means accepting all AI edits without reading them, which Karpathy calls fine for throwaway weekend projects.
- 2025-02-01 · [Evaluate models by making them play each other](ideas/2025-02-01-evaluate-models-by-making-them-play-games.md) — A game against another model adjusts its own difficulty, so one environment tests far more than a fixed question set does.
- 2025-01-30 · [LLMs need the practice problems of a textbook](ideas/2025-01-30-textbooks-exposition-worked-problems-practice.md) — LLMs got plenty of exposition and worked examples; practice problems with checkable answers are the new frontier, and they are RL.
- 2025-01-28 · [RL gives thinking models strategies you cannot write by hand](ideas/2025-01-28-cognitive-strategies-cannot-be-hand-programmed.md) — RL on reasoning models yields cognitive strategies, such as backtracking and analogies, so specify the goal, not the method.
- 2025-01-27 · [Filtering synthetic data is crude reinforcement learning](ideas/2025-01-27-synthetic-data-and-rl-are-one-loop.md) — Sampling answers and training on the best is trial-and-error learning in miniature; imitation teaches what humans know, trial and error finds what they do not. *(view)*
- 2025-01-17 · [People may train their minds the way they go to the gym](ideas/2025-01-17-minds-like-muscles-and-the-gym.md) — Machines made muscles unnecessary yet people still lift for pleasure and health; he expects people to keep training their minds for the same reasons. *(view)*
- 2025-01-02 · [A good assistant skips the lecture and the flattery](ideas/2025-01-02-llm-personality-no-lectures-no-flattery.md) — He wants best-effort problem solving without lectures, grandstanding, excess apology or fake praise; a chill, friend-like tone beats an HR-like one. *(view)*
- 2024-12-25 · [Cognitive load is what matters in software engineering](ideas/2024-12-25-cognitive-load-is-what-matters.md) — Karpathy endorses an essay that names cognitive load as the most true and least practiced view of good software.
- 2024-12-14 · [Judge an agent as you would a junior intern](ideas/2024-12-14-would-you-hire-it-as-a-junior-intern.md) — Judge agents by whether they can take an onboarding brief and finish a week-sized task, not by PhD-level puzzles.
- 2024-12-11 · [Read books together with an LLM, one chapter at a time](ideas/2024-12-11-read-books-with-an-llm.md) — Paste one chapter at a time into an LLM, ask for a summary, then read it yourself and ask questions; EPUB parses cleanly, so prefer it to PDF.
- 2024-11-29 · [Asking an AI is like asking the average data labeler](ideas/2024-11-29-asking-an-ai-is-asking-the-average-data-labeler.md) — A model's answer reflects a skilled, average data labeler distilled into weights, and RL changes this only where answers can be verified. *(view)*
- 2024-11-10 · [Hard closed problems are easy; long autonomous jobs are hard](ideas/2024-11-10-llms-solve-hard-prompts-but-fail-long-jobs.md) — LLMs solve hard problems served neatly in a prompt but struggle with long, coherent, autonomous work, and we need evals for that. *(view)*
- 2024-10-06 · [Break the shared LLM house voice with a style guide](ideas/2024-10-06-all-llms-sound-the-same.md) — Models overuse lists, 'multifaceted' and offers of help, all at the same length; an explicit style guide changes that.
- 2024-08-07 · [An LLM judge gets gamed when you optimise against it](ideas/2024-08-07-rlhf-is-just-barely-rl.md) — RLHF and LLM-graded RL optimise against a judge network, and the optimiser soon finds nonsense the judge scores highly; real RL needs rewards hard to game.
- 2024-03-12 · [Software engineering climbs an autonomy ladder like self-driving](ideas/2024-03-12-swe-autonomy-ladder-supervising-automation.md) — Coding tools move from lines to chunks to agents, so the work becomes supervising automation and oversight tools matter. *(view)*
- 2024-02-21 · [Build the thing, then build the ramp](ideas/2024-02-21-build-the-thing-then-build-the-ramp.md) — Code plus a README is not enough; a from-scratch explainer can bring ten to a hundred times more people to a project.
- 2024-02-10 · [Learning takes effort, unlike entertainment](ideas/2024-02-10-learning-is-not-supposed-to-be-fun.md) — Much educational short video is entertainment; real learning feels like effort, so use real sources, time, notes and rephrasing.
- 2024-01-20 · [The ideal training data is the thinking, not the final text](ideas/2024-01-20-ideal-training-data-is-your-thinking-process.md) — Models would learn most from the full sequence of thoughts and edits behind a text, not just the finished result. *(view)*
- 2024-01-12 · [Third-party models can hide sleeper agents](ideas/2024-01-12-sleeper-agent-llms-and-poisoned-models.md) — Poisoned training text or open weights can hide trigger phrases that safety finetuning may not remove, so treat models as part of your supply chain.
- 2023-12-08 · [Hallucination is the LLM's main feature, so the system must check it](ideas/2023-12-08-hallucination-is-the-llms-feature.md) — An LLM is a dream machine steered by prompts, so the system around it must check its output with search, tools and verification.
